destination.name: Hamilton (Victoria)
destination.tagline: A western Victoria wool town with a Guilfoyle garden and a waterfall nearby.
destination.description: Hamilton is a town in western Victoria on the Henty Highway, and calls itself the Wool Capital of the World. The surrounding shire produces as much as 15% of Australia's wool clip. The Botanic Gardens were designed in 1881 by William Guilfoyle, and Wannon Falls drops 30 m over basalt about 19 km west. Grampians National Park is a short drive away.

goodToKnow.title: Falls flow in winter
goodToKnow.detail: Wannon Falls is best in the winter wet and can shrink to a trickle by the end of summer.

goodToKnow.title: Reach it by road
goodToKnow.detail: Hamilton is on the Henty Highway and served by V/Line coaches. Its airport takes only recreational aircraft.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, when Wannon Falls is at its fullest after the winter rains.

notes: Months based only on Wannon Falls flow. Name 'Hamilton (Victoria)' collides with Hamilton NZ; owner to confirm the display name.
